# AstroSplat Render Modes
Also called: Basic and Enhanced modes

## Overview
AstroSplat Render Modes provide two distinct visualization strategies for rendering splat fields: Basic and Enhanced [S1, unofficial]. Basic mode uses a simpler splat presentation optimized for clarity and speed [S1, unofficial]. Enhanced mode is a perceptual rendering strategy featuring stronger depth cues and a richer volumetric feel, explicitly noted as not being a physical radiative model [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### Basic Mode
A rendering mode that simplifies the splat presentation to prioritize visual clarity and rendering speed [S1, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from Enhanced mode by favoring computational efficiency over perceptual depth cues [S1, unofficial]. Choose it for large datasets or interactive exploration where speed is paramount [S1, unofficial]. Link: Not provided in sources.

### Enhanced Mode
A perceptual rendering mode that applies stronger depth cues and adjusted blending to create a richer volumetric feel, explicitly not simulating physical radiative transfer [S1, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from Basic mode by prioritizing visual interpretability and depth perception [S1, unofficial]. Choose it for visualization requiring stronger depth cues and volumetric richness [S1, unofficial]. Link: Not provided in sources.

## Background
The AstroSplat Render Modes originate from the AstroSplat project, specifically the repository `VitorFigueiredoResearch/AstroSplat-Browser-native-volumetric-visualization-for-astrophysical-vector-fields` [S1, unofficial]. The project focuses on native volumetric visualization for astrophysical vector fields [S1, unofficial]. The dual-mode design allows users to toggle between the speed-focused Basic mode and the perceptual Enhanced mode [S1, unofficial].
